candidate.speaker: B
candidate.text: A tie is a perfectly good result. Can we leave it?

candidate.speaker: A
candidate.text: Not while I'm keeping score. We'll each get one minute and the same amount of icing.

candidate.speaker: B
candidate.text: I don't want to bake another cake. We already have two.

candidate.speaker: A
candidate.text: Then we'll ice a new border on each of those, blindfolded. Same minute; I'll have the judge compare the borders. You may skip the extra baking, but the lower score still gets the washing-up.

original.speaker: B
original.text: Why should anyone lose?

original.speaker: A
original.text: You can question the details after my decision. Otherwise this dinner ends without a distinction.

original.speaker: B
original.text: We both enjoyed it.

original.speaker: A
original.text: Then least enthusiastic enjoyment pays the tip. Rate yours carefully.

candidate.speaker: A
candidate.text: We've split the dinner bill exactly. I'll settle the tie with one more round: loser pays the tip.

candidate.speaker: B
candidate.text: Why should anyone lose? We both paid fairly.

candidate.speaker: A
candidate.text: Fairly gives us a tie. I'll accept a result that separates us; give me a criterion we can score.

candidate.speaker: B
candidate.text: We both enjoyed it. Isn't that enough?

candidate.speaker: A
candidate.text: Then rate your enjoyment from one to ten on a napkin. Fold it; we'll reveal together. The lower number pays the tip. I'll count even happiness properly before we leave.
